Subject: Dedicated reservation options for VectorScale deployment

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for the time today. Per our conversation I attached an initial dedicated offer (dedicated_offer_v1.pdf) and a short note on activation. High level we wanted to give you three pragmatic paths so your infra and procurement teams can evaluate trade-offs between unit cost and operational predictability: a small starter footprint, a growth band, and a scalable enterprise lane.

Quick asks from our side:
- Can you confirm your Q3 production target for model throughput (tokens/sec) or an expected daily token volume?
- Is there an internal procurement milestone (PO or security review) that would cap the activation window?

I’m looping Ben (sales engineer) and Karthik (solutions) to follow up with a short matrix. We can schedule a 30-min call next week to walk the options and map to your timeline.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

marissa@redwoodinference.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options for VectorScale deployment

Marissa —

Thanks for the materials. A couple quick clarifications from our side before the call:
1) Minimum guaranteed GPUs — our procurement team wants to avoid large minimums but also needs predictable baseline for SLA. Can you outline what minimums you typically require and whether they can be reduced over an initial pilot?
2) Ramp cadence — how flexible are ramp months? We may want a front-loaded pilot in June and then a 3-month ramp to production.
3) Autoscale vs reserved mix — we prefer a small reserved floor plus burstable pool; how do credits/pricing look for bursts?

Evan and procurement are copied. If you can send a one-page comparison matrix before the call that would be helpful.

Cheers,
Sofia Ramos
VP of Product | VectorScale Robotics
sofia.ramos@vectorscale.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Ramos <sofia.ramos@vectorscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-14T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options for VectorScale deployment

Sofia —

Appended below is a concise matrix that should answer Procurement and Eng's questions. I attached a spreadsheet (vectorscale_dedicated_options.xlsx) with the same numbers and an estimated monthly burn model.

Option A — Starter Pilot (recommended for proof-of-value)- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 8 (reserved)- Typical burst cap: +8 GPUs on-demand (burst credits available)- Ramp: single-month activation window (pilot month), convert to Growth or decommit with 30 days notice- Warm-up credits: 250 GPU-hours to use in pilot month- Suggested commitment term: 3 months (pilot -> decision)- Unit pricing (committed): $3.50 / GPU-hour; burst price (on-demand): $5.20 / GPU-hour

Option B — Growth Lane (balance of cost and predictability)- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 32 (reserved)- Burst cap: +32 GPUs (conditional on capacity)- Ramp: 2-month staged activation (16 -> 32) with optional mid-month top-ups- Warm-up credits: 1,000 GPU-hours spread across first 60 days- Suggested commitment term: 12 months- Unit pricing (committed): $2.90 / GPU-hour; burst price: $4.40 / GPU-hour

Option C — Enterprise Slate (throughput-first, lowest unit cost)- Minimum guaranteed GPUs: 128 (reserved)- Burst cap: +64 GPUs via reserved buffer & cross-region fallback- Ramp: 3–6 month phased ramp with weekly checkpoints and runbook- Warm-up credits: 6,000 GPU-hours across onboarding- Suggested commitment term: 24 months + SLA banding- Unit pricing (committed): $2.30 / GPU-hour; burst price: $3.80 / GPU-hour

Additional notes / operational controls:
- Autoscale: continuous batching and prefix caching remain active; reserved pool is for base latency-sensitive traffic. Bursts are handled by on-demand lanes where available.
- Fallbacks: we can route to quantized variants or lower-cost model families automatically if capacity is constrained (policy configurable).
- Billing: monthly, with token-level cost breakout by model/route. Billing credits for pilot convert to account credit if a Growth or Enterprise contract is signed within 60 days.
- Procurement: we support PO and Net-30 invoicing; enterprise legal prefers a 30–60 day signature window for SOW attachments.

Attachments included: 2026-05-14_vectorscale_dedicated_options.xlsx, 2026-05-14_dedicated_terms_summary.pdf

If helpful, we can present the matrix in a 20-minute internal/demo call focused on procurement questions.

—Karthik
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Karthik / Marissa —

This is very helpful. A few follow-ups before we present to Procurement:
- For Option B (Growth Lane), what's the penalty / decommit profile if we need to reduce from 32 to 16 after 6 months? Is there a ramp-down schedule?
- Can burst credits be pooled across regions? We run tests in US-west and occasionally in EU-west; pooling would help utilization.
- Pilot convert credit: can that be applied against the first three months of billing for Growth?

Procurement also asked for a simple mutual action plan with milestones (PO, SOC2 assurance pack, security questionnaire completion, activation date). Could you draft that and we’ll align timelines on our side.

Sofia
